entries.label: Closed contour
entries.description: Whether the contour encloses a fillable region.

entries.label: Sample points
entries.description: Number of points in the polyline used by this analysis snapshot.

entries.label: Logical edges
entries.description: Semantic edges before each edge is subdivided for rendering and analysis.

entries.label: Compactness
entries.description: 4πA/P²; one for an ideal circle and lower for less compact forms.

entries.label: Solidity
entries.description: Contour area divided by convex-hull area.

entries.label: Convexity
entries.description: Convex-hull perimeter divided by contour perimeter.

entries.label: Radial tangent alignment
entries.description: Tangent dot radial direction: negative inward, zero circumferential, positive outward.

entries.label: Outward normal vs center
entries.description: Outward normal dot radial direction: negative center-facing, positive away from center.

entries.label: Reader contact rank
entries.description: Zero-based order along the active reader, independent of stable contact identity.

entries.label: Reader incidence angle
entries.description: Acute angle between reader and contour tangent: zero is grazing; π/2 is transverse.

entries.label: Reader transversality
entries.description: Absolute reader/tangent cross product: zero near tangency and one at a right-angle crossing.

entries.label: Inside fraction
entries.availability: closed contour with finite reader extent

entries.label: Minimum transversality
entries.availability: line or ray reader with contacts
entries.description: Smallest contact transversality; values near zero flag a sampled tangency candidate.

entries.label: Mean transversality
entries.availability: line or ray reader with contacts

entries.label: Contact splits
entries.description: A one-to-many identity event; intentionally unavailable until split semantics are implemented.

entries.label: Contact merges
entries.description: A many-to-one identity event; intentionally unavailable until merge semantics are implemented.

entries.name: Swing clock warp
entries.syntax: fn swingTime(straightTime: f32, swing: f32) -> f32
entries.audio: Alternates long and short sequencer steps while keeping each two-step pair on the same overall clock.
entries.note: The live synth clamps swing to 0–0.42. The input and output are measured in sequencer steps, not seconds.

entries.name: Sequence lane lookup
entries.syntax: fn laneValue(step: u32, lane: u32) -> f32
entries.audio: Reads one normalized control cell from the 64-step × 8-lane score buffer.
entries.note: Step and lane indices are bounded before the flattened buffer read. Values are sanitized to 0–1 on upload.

entries.name: Step index
entries.syntax: fn sequenceStepAt(time: f32) -> u32
entries.audio: Turns absolute seconds into the current looped sequencer step after swing.
entries.note: The active pattern can be 4–64 steps and the clock can run at 0.25–20 steps per second.

entries.name: Normalized lane routing
entries.syntax: fn routedUnit(step: u32, nextStep: u32, phase: f32, destination: u32, fallback: f32, amount: f32) -> f32
entries.audio: Interpolates a routed lane between steps and blends it into a normalized 0–1 synth parameter.
entries.execution: Per sample · up to 6 lane reads
entries.note: The current shader uses 78% routing depth for most destinations; duplicate destinations compound in lane order.

entries.name: Unit-to-physical mapping
entries.syntax: fn routedRange(..., fallback: f32, minimum: f32, maximum: f32, amount: f32) -> f32
entries.audio: Maps a 0–1 modulation lane into seconds, hertz, drive, gain, or another physical range.
entries.note: The mapping is linear. Filter cutoff modulation is therefore linear in hertz rather than perceptually logarithmic.

entries.name: Scale-degree lookup
entries.syntax: fn modeDegree(degree: u32, scale: u32) -> f32
entries.audio: Returns a semitone interval for Dorian, Phrygian, or harmonic-minor scale degrees.
entries.note: The helper covers the three seven-note modes; chromatic, whole-tone, and quarter-tone mappings live in scaleNote.

entries.name: Pitch quantizer
entries.syntax: fn scaleNote(normalized: f32, scaleValue: f32) -> f32
entries.audio: Quantizes a normalized lane into a semitone offset in one of six tuning maps.
entries.note: Available maps are chromatic, Dorian, Phrygian, harmonic minor, whole tone, and quarter-tone.

entries.name: MIDI to frequency
entries.syntax: fn midiFrequency(note: f32) -> f32 { return 440.0 * pow(2.0, (note - 69.0) / 12.0); }
entries.audio: Converts note numbers—including fractional notes—into oscillator frequency in hertz.
entries.note: Pitch glide is performed in note space before this conversion, producing an exponential frequency glide.

entries.name: Quintic smoothing
entries.syntax: fn smootherstep01(value: f32) -> f32
entries.audio: Makes a click-resistant 0→1 transition with zero slope and curvature at both ends.
entries.note: The exact curve is x³(x(6x−15)+10) after clamping to 0–1.

entries.name: Deterministic hash noise
entries.syntax: fn hash11(value: f32) -> f32
entries.audio: Produces repeatable pseudo-random values for noise, jitter, modal scatter, grain position, and reverb taps.
entries.note: Returns approximately 0–1 and is not a stateful PRNG. The synth seed is clamped to 1–65535.

entries.name: Rational soft clip
entries.syntax: fn softClip(value: vec2<f32>) -> vec2<f32> { return value / (vec2(1.0) + abs(value)); }
entries.audio: Compresses peaks smoothly toward ±1, adding harmonics without a hard digital corner.
entries.note: This is a rational saturator, not tanh. It changes level as well as tone, so gain staging still matters.

entries.name: Spectral Acid
entries.syntax: fn spectralAcid(t: f32, local: f32, frequency: f32, timbre: f32, motion: f32, macros: vec4<f32>) -> vec2<f32>
entries.audio: Builds an acid-like tone from 1–48 harmonics under a moving spectral cutoff and resonance peak.
entries.note: This is spectral weighting, not a recursive resonant filter. High partials fade as they approach Nyquist.

entries.name: Classic FM / PM network
entries.syntax: fn classicFm(t: f32, local: f32, frequency: f32, timbre: f32, motion: f32, macros: vec4<f32>) -> vec2<f32>
entries.audio: Creates sideband-rich tones with nested sine phase offsets, a second carrier, and an optional sub oscillator.
entries.note: The UI calls it FM, while the shader expression is the phase-modulation form sin(phase + modulator × index).

entries.name: Wavefold Table
entries.syntax: fn wavefoldTable(t: f32, local: f32, frequency: f32, timbre: f32, motion: f32, macros: vec4<f32>) -> vec2<f32>
entries.audio: Scans analytic sine→triangle→saw shapes, detunes 1–8 layers, then folds them through a sine.
entries.note: Layer gain is normalized by √count. Analytic saws and strong nonlinear folding can alias.

entries.name: Modal Metal
entries.syntax: fn modalMetal(t: f32, local: f32, frequency: f32, timbre: f32, motion: f32, macros: vec4<f32>) -> vec2<f32>
entries.audio: Sums 1–32 slightly scattered, inharmonic sine modes with independent onset and damping.
entries.note: Mode ratios follow n + 0.018n² with seeded scatter. A spectral fade protects the upper band.

entries.name: Particle Cloud
entries.syntax: fn particleCloud(t: f32, local: f32, frequency: f32, timbre: f32, motion: f32, macros: vec4<f32>) -> vec2<f32>
entries.audio: Layers 1–16 windowed, detuned oscillator particles with held hash grit and seeded stereo positions.
entries.note: It is synthetic granular sound, not sample playback. The grit value changes every 12 samples.

entries.name: Additive Organ
entries.syntax: fn additiveOrgan(t: f32, local: f32, frequency: f32, timbre: f32, motion: f32, macros: vec4<f32>) -> vec2<f32>
entries.audio: Sums nine editable drawbar-like ranks, each with its own ratio, level, AM rate, and AM depth.
entries.execution: Per sample · rank loop + buffer reads
entries.note: Ratios span 0.125–16×, AM 0–30 Hz. Built-in chorale and rotor motions add slow phase and stereo movement.

entries.name: Vector Wavetable
entries.syntax: fn vectorWavetable(t: f32, local: f32, frequency: f32, timbre: f32, motion: f32, macros: vec4<f32>) -> vec2<f32>
entries.audio: Reconstructs sine, triangle, and saw spectra from up to 64 harmonics, then morphs between them.
entries.note: Despite the name, this is analytic Fourier reconstruction rather than texture or buffer lookup.

entries.name: Formant Bank
entries.syntax: fn formantBank(t: f32, local: f32, frequency: f32, timbre: f32, motion: f32, macros: vec4<f32>) -> vec2<f32>
entries.audio: Weights 1–12 source harmonics with three moving Gaussian peaks to suggest vowel-like spectra.
entries.note: This is spectral-envelope synthesis, not a bank of recursive formant filters.

entries.name: Model dispatch
entries.syntax: fn synthModel(model: u32, ...) -> vec2<f32>
entries.audio: Selects one of the eight synthesis algorithms for a layer.
entries.note: Model IDs are 0–7. In the current engine each layer owns its model selection.

entries.name: Layer renderer
entries.syntax: fn renderLayer(layer: vec4<f32>, time: f32, local: f32, frequency: f32, ...) -> vec2<f32>
entries.audio: Renders one model and applies its semitone detune, level, and stereo pan.
entries.note: A layer record is vec4(model, level, detune, pan); detune spans ±24 semitones and pan spans −1…1.

entries.name: Stack / equal-power morph
entries.syntax: fn layeredSound(..., morph: f32) -> vec2<f32>
entries.audio: Either sums up to six layers with level normalization or crossfades adjacent layers at near-constant power.
entries.execution: Per sample · up to 6 model calls
entries.note: Morph weights are cos(xπ/2) and sin(xπ/2). Stack normalization uses the square root of summed layer levels.

entries.name: Dry signal graph
entries.syntax: fn drySound(time: f32) -> vec2<f32>
entries.audio: Composes clock, pitch, glide, click-safe envelope, routed macros, layered synthesis, orbit pan, drive, and limiting.
entries.note: Oscillator-local time retriggers each step. Attack and release edges are at most 12 ms and suppress reset clicks.

entries.name: Circular history read
entries.syntax: fn historyAt(absoluteSample: u32, delaySamples: u32) -> vec2<f32>
entries.audio: Reads an earlier stereo sample from the persistent eight-second ring buffer.
entries.note: Reads before time zero return silence. This history contains the dry signal written by pass one.

entries.name: Windowed-sinc FIR low-pass
entries.syntax: fn sincLowpass(absoluteSample: u32, cutoffHz: f32) -> vec2<f32>
entries.audio: Removes frequencies above the cutoff with a finite, causal, Hann-windowed impulse response.
entries.note: The UI forces odd tap counts. At 31 taps the group delay is at most 15 samples.

entries.name: Feed-forward multi-tap delay
entries.syntax: fn multiTapDelay(absoluteSample: u32, delayTime: f32) -> vec2<f32>
entries.audio: Adds one to four decaying echoes with odd taps swapped left-to-right.
entries.note: Tap spacing is 10 ms–1.5 s and decay is 0–0.88. This is feed-forward; there is no feedback loop.

entries.name: Clip / fold waveshaper
entries.syntax: fn postWaveshaper(value: vec2<f32>, drive: f32, fold: f32) -> vec2<f32>
entries.audio: Drives the signal, then morphs from rational soft clipping into repeated sine folding.
entries.note: Drive spans 1–16× and fold 0–1. Nonlinear output can alias, especially on already bright material.

entries.name: Sparse convolution reverb
entries.syntax: fn convolutionReverb(absoluteSample: u32, size: f32, decay: f32) -> vec2<f32>
entries.audio: Sums 4–64 scattered, decaying history reads into a stereo reflection cloud.
entries.note: It is deterministic sparse convolution, not FFT convolution or a loaded room impulse response. Nominal size is 0.08–4 s.

entries.name: Dry compute pass
entries.syntax: @compute @workgroup_size(WORKGROUP_SIZE) fn synthesizeDry(@builtin(global_invocation_id) global_id: vec3<u32>)
entries.audio: Renders one stereo sample per invocation, writes the dry chunk, and records it in persistent history.
entries.note: The sample index comes from global_invocation_id.x. The host overrides workgroup size and sample rate.

entries.name: Effects compute pass
entries.syntax: @compute @workgroup_size(WORKGROUP_SIZE) fn processFx(@builtin(global_invocation_id) global_id: vec3<u32>)
entries.audio: Applies routed FIR filtering, feed-forward delay, waveshaping, sparse reverb, and a final safety limit.
entries.note: Delay and reverb read dry history; the shaper acts on the accumulated mix. It is not a fully serial conventional pedal chain.

entries.name: Sample-accurate clock
entries.syntax: let t = time_info.offset + f32(sample) / SAMPLE_RATE;
entries.audio: Gives every output sample an absolute time in seconds—the common coordinate for oscillators, envelopes, and modulation.
entries.note: SAMPLE_RATE must match the playback AudioContext. Absolute time preserves continuity across GPU chunks.

entries.name: Phase + basic oscillators
entries.audio: Turns a cyclic 0–1 phase into sine, triangle, or saw waveforms.
entries.note: The analytic triangle and saw are not band-limited; fade or oversample their upper harmonics to reduce aliasing.

entries.name: Pulse / comparator
entries.syntax: let pulse = select(-1.0, 1.0, phase < duty);
entries.audio: Creates a square or variable-width pulse; at control rate it becomes a gate and rhythmic mask.
entries.note: The discontinuity aliases at audio rate. Smooth edges, additive reconstruction, or oversampling are safer for bright pitches.

entries.name: Ring modulation
entries.syntax: let ring = carrier * modulator;
entries.audio: Replaces the original pitches with sum-and-difference sidebands, often producing bells, clangs, and shifting beating.
entries.note: A bipolar modulator suppresses the carrier; a unipolar one behaves more like tremolo and retains it.

entries.name: Amplitude modulation / tremolo
entries.syntax: let tremolo = signal * mix(1.0, 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(t * rate * TAU), depth);
entries.audio: Moves loudness periodically; slow rates pulse, while audio rates create AM sidebands.
entries.note: Depth 0–1 keeps the example unipolar. Audio-rate use needs headroom because new sidebands can increase peaks.

entries.name: Hard oscillator sync
entries.syntax:
let master = fract(t * masterHz);
let synced = sin(fract(master * ratio) * TAU);
entries.audio: Forces one oscillator cycle structure to restart with another, producing swept, cutting upper harmonics.
entries.note: Resets are discontinuous and alias easily. A splice envelope or band-limited correction improves high-register use.

entries.name: Sample + hold
entries.syntax: let held = hash11(floor(t * rate)) * 2.0 - 1.0;
entries.audio: Produces random plateaus at a chosen update rate for stepped pitch, timbre, pan, or grain control.
entries.note: Because the value is derived from time, it is deterministic and needs no mutable state. Smooth it when discontinuities would click.

entries.name: Amplitude quantizer / bit crush
entries.syntax: let crushed = round(signal * levels) / levels;
entries.audio: Reduces amplitude resolution into audible steps, adding digital grit and inharmonic error.
entries.note: Keep levels above zero. Pairing with sample-rate reduction requires history or a time-derived hold index.

entries.name: Equal-power stereo pan
entries.syntax:
let angle = (clamp(pan, -1.0, 1.0) + 1.0) * PI * 0.25;
let stereo = vec2(signal * cos(angle), signal * sin(angle));
entries.audio: Places a mono source across stereo while keeping perceived power steadier near the center.
entries.note: The live shader mostly uses amplitude-offset panning and phase spread; this is a useful alternative primitive.

entries.name: FIR high-pass by subtraction
entries.syntax: let high = historyAt(n, centerTap) - sincLowpass(n, cutoffHz);
entries.audio: Keeps the spectral material above the cutoff by subtracting a time-aligned low-pass result.
entries.note: The dry path must be delayed by the FIR center tap before subtraction or phase mismatch will spoil the response.

entries.name: FIR band-pass by difference
entries.syntax: let band = sincLowpass(n, highHz) - sincLowpass(n, lowHz);
entries.audio: Isolates a frequency band between two cutoffs.
entries.note: Both filters need the same tap count and alignment. The cost is roughly twice one low-pass.

entries.name: Uploaded wavetable lookup
entries.audio: Reads an arbitrary periodic shape from a storage buffer and interpolates between samples.
entries.note: The current Vector Wavetable reconstructs spectra analytically; it does not yet upload or read arbitrary tables.

entries.name: Trigger / unit impulse
entries.syntax: let impulse = select(0.0, 1.0, sampleIndex == eventSample);
entries.audio: Marks one exact sample as an excitation: the smallest possible click, drum trigger, convolution probe, or resonator strike.
entries.note: A single-sample impulse is extremely bright. Feed it into a resonator or window it when an exposed click is not the goal.

entries.name: Exponential decay envelope
entries.syntax: let env = exp(-max(localTime, 0.0) * decayRate);
entries.audio: Produces the fast attack and curved energy loss associated with plucks, struck objects, and electronic percussion.
entries.note: Choose decayRate from a desired time constant. Clamp or gate the tail if denormally small values waste work.

entries.name: Segment / ADSR envelope
entries.syntax: fn adsr(t: f32, gate: f32, a: f32, d: f32, s: f32, r: f32) -> f32 { /* piecewise ramps */ }
entries.audio: Shapes a note through attack, decay, sustain, and release, or through any sequence of breakpoint segments.
entries.note: The shader must know note-local time and release time. Smooth segment joins or use exponential curves to avoid slope discontinuities.

entries.name: Hann / Gaussian grain window
entries.syntax: let hann = 0.5 - 0.5 * cos(TAU * clamp(grainPhase, 0.0, 1.0));
entries.audio: Fades both ends of a short event so grains, loops, and model changes splice without clicks.
entries.note: Hann reaches zero at both ends; Gaussian windows trade exact zero endpoints for a more concentrated spectrum.

entries.name: Bitmask rhythm sequencer
entries.syntax: let hit = ((pattern >> (step & 31u)) & 1u) != 0u;
entries.audio: Stores a 32-step gate pattern inside one integer and reveals one rhythmic bit at a time.
entries.note: Bit order is a design choice. Longer patterns can use several u32 values or a storage-buffer bit field.

entries.name: Interpolated value noise
entries.syntax:
let x = t * rate;
let drift = mix(hash11(floor(x)), hash11(floor(x) + 1.0), smootherstep01(fract(x)));
entries.audio: Turns discrete seeded randomness into continuous wandering control or smooth procedural noise.
entries.note: This is value noise rather than white noise. Its bandwidth follows the lattice rate and its exact spectrum depends on the interpolation curve.

entries.name: Chirp / swept oscillator
entries.syntax: let chirp = sin(TAU * (startHz * t + 0.5 * hzPerSecond * t * t));
entries.audio: Sweeps frequency continuously; short downward curves make kicks and impacts, while long sweeps scan resonances.
entries.note: Integrate frequency into phase as shown. Substituting a changing frequency directly into sin(TAU * t * f(t)) changes the intended sweep law.

entries.name: Unison / supersaw bank
entries.syntax: for (var voice = 0u; voice < voiceCount; voice++) { sum += saw(fract(t * hz * detune[voice] + phase[voice])); }
entries.audio: Stacks many slightly detuned oscillators into a wide, beating, high-energy source.
entries.note: Raw saw layers alias and correlated phases create large peaks. Band-limit, phase-scatter, and normalize by voice count or power.

entries.name: Analytic plucked-string series
entries.syntax: for (var h = 1u; h <= 50u; h++) { y += pluckAmp(h, position) * exp(-damping(h) * t) * sin(TAU * modeHz(h, stiffness) * t); }
entries.audio: Models a plucked string as damped modes whose amplitudes depend on pluck position and whose frequencies bend with stiffness.
entries.note: Unlike Karplus–Strong, this closed-form ShaderToy technique needs no recursive delay. Fade modes above Nyquist and bound the loop for WebGPU.

entries.name: Phase-distortion oscillator
entries.syntax:
let warpedPhase = select(phase * pivot / split, pivot + (phase - split) * (1.0 - pivot) / (1.0 - split), phase >= split);
let y = sin(TAU * warpedPhase);
entries.audio: Bends oscillator phase before waveform lookup, changing harmonic content while keeping the fundamental cycle locked.
entries.note: Keep split away from 0 and 1. Sharp changes in phase slope create bright spectra and may need oversampling.

entries.name: Wave-terrain scan
entries.syntax:
let p = vec2(cos(TAU * phase), sin(TAU * phase)) * radius + center;
let y = terrainSample(p);
entries.audio: Moves a periodic orbit across a 2D height field and interprets the sampled elevation as a waveform.
entries.note: Interpolation, terrain resolution, and path continuity control aliasing. A texture or storage buffer must supply the field.

entries.name: Bytebeat / integer formula
entries.syntax:
let byte = (sample * ((sample >> 5u) | (sample >> 8u))) & 255u;
let y = f32(byte) / 127.5 - 1.0;
entries.audio: Turns integer overflow, shifts, masks, and bitwise logic into self-organizing lo-fi melody and rhythm.
entries.note: WGSL integer widths and precedence should be explicit. The 8-bit output is intentionally discontinuous, aliased, and DC-prone.

entries.name: Fixed-iteration chaotic recurrence
entries.syntax:
var x = seed + sin(t * rate);
for (var i = 0u; i < 8u; i++) { x = 1.3 / max(abs(x), 0.001) - 1.0; }
entries.audio: Maps a bounded nonlinear recurrence into brittle tones, squelches, discontinuities, and deterministic pseudo-chaos.
entries.note: Clamp singularities and keep iteration counts fixed or tightly bounded. Tiny parameter changes can create large level and bandwidth changes.

entries.name: Procedural kick drum
entries.syntax:
let phase = TAU * (bodyHz * t + bendHz * (1.0 - exp(-pitchDecay * t)) / pitchDecay);
let kick = sin(phase) * exp(-ampDecay * t);
entries.audio: Combines a rapidly falling oscillator pitch with a slower amplitude decay to create a kick-like impact and body.
entries.note: The phase integrates the exponential frequency bend. Add a separately windowed click rather than forcing the body oscillator to supply all attack energy.

entries.name: Procedural snare drum
entries.syntax: let snare = noise(t) * exp(-noiseDecay * t) + sin(TAU * bodyHz * t) * exp(-bodyDecay * t);
entries.audio: Layers a short noisy shell or wire burst over a lower decaying tonal body.
entries.note: Band-shaping the noise matters more than adding more noise. Separate transient, body, and tail envelopes keep the result controllable.

entries.name: Metallic hi-hat / cymbal bank
entries.syntax:
for (var i = 0u; i < 6u; i++) { metal += sign(sin(TAU * t * baseHz * ratios[i])); }
let hat = highShape(metal) * exp(-decay * t);
entries.audio: Uses inharmonic pulse or sine components, high-frequency emphasis, and a short decay to suggest metal plates and hats.
entries.note: Square-like components alias aggressively. Sine banks or band-limited pulses are cleaner; a zero-mean high-band stage prevents excessive DC and thump.

entries.name: Clap burst train
entries.syntax:
let bursts = window(t, 0.000, 0.018) + 0.8 * window(t, 0.026, 0.016) + 0.6 * window(t, 0.052, 0.020);
let clap = noise(t) * bursts;
entries.audio: Shapes filtered noise into several closely spaced attacks followed by an optional diffuse tail.
entries.note: Keep burst timing in seconds and soften every window edge. Filtering or differentiating the noise moves the apparent hand size and distance.

entries.name: Sample playback + interpolation
entries.syntax:
let x = start + playhead * rate;
let y = mix(samples[u32(floor(x))], samples[u32(floor(x)) + 1u], fract(x));
entries.audio: Reads recorded audio at a movable rate; negative or wrapped playheads enable reverse, loop, and scrubbing behaviors.
entries.note: Bounds, channel layout, interpolation quality, and resampling alias control are engine responsibilities. Cubic reads cost more but reduce interpolation roughness.

entries.name: Sample-granular cloud
entries.syntax: for (var g = 0u; g < grainCount; g++) { sum += sampleAt(grainStart[g] + grainPhase[g] * rate[g]) * grainWindow(grainPhase[g]); }
entries.audio: Overlaps many short, independently positioned sample fragments into clouds, freezes, swarms, and time-stretched textures.
entries.execution: Per sample · bounded random buffer gathers
entries.note: A modest grain count fits one invocation; very large clouds need a separate grain-parallel pass and mix reduction. Random reads can be bandwidth-heavy.

entries.name: FOF / formant grain
entries.syntax: let fof = sin(TAU * formantHz * local) * exp(-bandwidth * local) * grainWindow(local / duration);
entries.audio: A short exponentially damped sinusoidal grain that becomes a vowel-like formant when repeated at a pitched rate.
entries.note: FOF synthesis separates the pulse repetition pitch from each grain's formant frequency and bandwidth.

entries.name: Sample-rate reducer
entries.syntax:
let heldIndex = (sampleIndex / holdSamples) * holdSamples;
let reduced = history[heldIndex % historySize];
entries.audio: Holds samples for several output frames, producing images, stepped transients, and clocked digital roughness.
entries.note: This changes time resolution, unlike amplitude bit crushing. A stateless source can instead be reevaluated at quantized time.

entries.name: Polynomial / Chebyshev shaper
entries.syntax:
let x = clamp(signal, -1.0, 1.0);
let third = 4.0 * x * x * x - 3.0 * x;
entries.audio: Maps amplitude through a polynomial; Chebyshev terms can emphasize chosen harmonics for a sine input.
entries.note: The harmonic guarantee holds only for a properly scaled sine. General signals create intermodulation, and every nonlinear map can alias.

entries.name: Rectification / frequency doubling
entries.syntax: let rectified = abs(signal) * 2.0 - 1.0;
entries.audio: Folds negative waveform halves upward, strongly emphasizing even harmonics and doubling a sine's apparent cycle rate.
entries.note: The raw abs output carries DC; the centered example assumes a normalized source and may still need a DC blocker after asymmetric inputs.

entries.name: Constant-power crossfade
entries.syntax:
let angle = clamp(morph, 0.0, 1.0) * PI * 0.5;
let y = a * cos(angle) + b * sin(angle);
entries.audio: Moves between two signals with steadier energy than a linear fade when the sources are uncorrelated.
entries.note: Correlated sources can still reinforce or cancel. Linear interpolation may be preferable when morphing two aligned versions of one waveform.

entries.name: Mid / side matrix
entries.audio: Separates the stereo center from the difference signal so width and spatial processing can be controlled independently.
entries.note: Extreme side gain can reduce mono compatibility and increase peaks. Decode with the same normalization convention used for encoding.

entries.name: Fractional delay interpolation
entries.audio: Reads between stored samples so delay time, pitch-like comb spacing, and moving spatial cues can vary smoothly.
entries.note: Linear interpolation attenuates high frequencies at fractional positions. Cubic or all-pass interpolation trades more work for a flatter response.

entries.name: Feed-forward chorus / flanger
entries.audio: Mixes a signal with a slowly moving short delay, creating detuned doubles, comb motion, and ensemble width.
entries.execution: Per sample · history gather · no recursion
entries.note: This feed-forward form fits independent output samples. Adding feedback moves it into ordered-state territory.

entries.name: Doppler / moving delay read
entries.syntax:
let distance = length(sourcePosition(t) - listenerPosition);
let y = fractionalHistoryRead(n, distance * sampleRate / speedOfSound);
entries.audio: Turns changing source distance into a variable propagation delay, producing natural pitch shift and motion cues.
entries.execution: Per sample · position math + history gather
entries.note: Rapid delay changes can click or exceed available history. Smooth trajectories, enforce causal bounds, and model attenuation separately.

entries.name: Bounded polyphonic voice bank
entries.syntax:
for (var voice = 0u; voice < activeVoices; voice++) { mixOut += renderVoice(voice, t); }
mixOut *= inverseSqrt(max(f32(activeVoices), 1.0));
entries.audio: Renders many notes, partial groups, or events into one sample while keeping their control records in GPU buffers.
entries.note: This is simple for tens of voices. Hundreds or thousands are better dispatched voice-parallel and reduced in a second pass.

entries.name: First-order ambisonic encode
entries.syntax: let bFormat = signal * vec4(0.7071, cos(azimuth) * cos(elevation), sin(azimuth) * cos(elevation), sin(elevation));
entries.audio: Represents one mono source as an omnidirectional component plus three directional components for later spatial decoding.
entries.note: Channel order and normalization conventions vary. The engine must retain four or more channels until a speaker or binaural decode stage.

entries.name: PolyBLEP / polynomial edge correction
entries.syntax:
let dt = hz / sampleRate;
let saw = 2.0 * phase - 1.0 - polyBlep(phase, dt);
entries.audio: Cancels much of the aliasing around saw, pulse, and hard-sync discontinuities with a short polynomial correction.
entries.note: PolyBLEP corrects value jumps; PolyBLAMP or higher-order polynomial transition regions address slope jumps. Clamp dt and handle both pulse edges.

entries.name: Log-frequency parameter map
entries.syntax: let hz = minimumHz * pow(maximumHz / minimumHz, clamp(unit, 0.0, 1.0));
entries.audio: Maps a normalized control evenly across octaves rather than spending most of its travel on the top of a hertz range.
entries.note: Both bounds must be positive. The live routedRange helper is linear, so this is the preferable primitive for cutoff, rate, and frequency controls.

entries.name: Event-relative AR / release guard
entries.syntax: let env = smoothstep(0.0, attack, timeSinceHit) * smoothstep(0.0, release, timeToNextHit) * exp2(-decay * timeSinceHit);
entries.audio: Gives every irregular trigger a click-safe onset, decay, and pre-emptive release before the following event.
entries.note: The sequencer must provide both time since the previous hit and time until the next. Guard empty patterns and zero-duration segments.

entries.name: Euclidean rhythm predicate
entries.syntax: let hit = ((step * pulses) % steps) < pulses;
entries.audio: Distributes a chosen number of onsets as evenly as possible across a repeating number of steps.
entries.note: Require 0 < pulses <= steps. Rotating the step index changes the accent position without changing the spacing family.

entries.name: Phase-correct exponential pitch glide
entries.syntax:
let phaseCycles = startHz * (pow(2.0, octavesPerSecond * t) - 1.0) / (octavesPerSecond * log(2.0));
let y = sin(TAU * phaseCycles);
entries.audio: Glides linearly in octaves or semitones while keeping oscillator phase continuous and instantaneous pitch correct.
entries.note: Special-case a near-zero glide rate to avoid division by zero, and append the final constant-frequency phase after a finite glide segment.

entries.name: Rounded saw / square edge
entries.audio: Rounds a waveform discontinuity into a one-knob family that sounds progressively softer and filter-like.
entries.note: This ShaderToy idiom is not a general filter and is not fully band-limited. Clamp roundness below one and prefer PolyBLEP for stronger alias suppression.

entries.name: Analytic transfer response on partials
entries.syntax:
let h = transferAt(partialHz, cutoffHz, resonance);
sum += partialAmp * h.magnitude * sin(partialPhase - h.phase);
entries.audio: Applies a filter's complex magnitude and phase response directly to each known synthesized harmonic without a recursive audio stream.
entries.note: This can mimic resonant ladder-like coloration only when the input is an explicit partial sum. It cannot filter arbitrary recorded audio without history or an FFT.

entries.name: Cyclic fractal noise
entries.syntax:
var p = vec3<f32>(t, t * 1.7, t * 2.3);
for (var octave = 0u; octave < 5u; octave++) { p = rotation * p + sin(p.zxy); sum += cross(cos(p), sin(p.yzx)); p *= 1.8; }
entries.audio: Creates coherent, structured procedural noise that can sound airy, granular, tonal, or liquid rather than uniformly random.
entries.execution: Per sample · fixed trig-heavy octave loop
entries.note: The field may carry tonal peaks or DC bias and is relatively expensive. Reduce large time coordinates before trigonometry to preserve f32 precision.

entries.name: Box–Muller Gaussian pair
entries.syntax:
let radius = sqrt(-2.0 * log(max(uniform.x, 1e-6)));
let gaussian = radius * vec2(cos(TAU * uniform.y), sin(TAU * uniform.y));
entries.audio: Turns uniform hashes into bell-shaped random values for natural detune, spatial scatter, modal variation, and grain placement.
entries.note: Never pass zero to log. Seed by event, voice, or grain so values remain fixed for that object's lifetime unless noise is intended.

entries.name: Control-derived ducking
entries.syntax:
let duck = smoothstep(0.0, recover, timeSinceKick) * smoothstep(0.0, guard, timeToNextKick);
let y = source * mix(floorGain, 1.0, duck);
entries.audio: Creates sidechain-like pumping directly from a known trigger clock without measuring an audio signal.
entries.note: This is deterministic gain choreography, not a compressor. It cannot react to unexpected input levels, but it avoids envelope-detection state.

entries.name: DC blocker / one-pole filter
entries.audio: Removes very-low-frequency offset introduced by asymmetrical waveshaping, rectification, or modulation.
entries.note: Each output depends on the previous output. A serial lane, parallel prefix scan, or block state-space form is required.

entries.name: True feedback delay
entries.syntax: y[n] = x[n] + feedback * y[n - delaySamples];
entries.audio: Recirculates echoes so they evolve, saturate, filter, or destabilize over time.
entries.note: The live multi-tap delay is feed-forward. Feedback needs ordered state, ping-pong blocks, or a delay long enough to break dependencies across dispatches.

entries.name: Comb + all-pass network
entries.syntax:
comb = x[n] + g * comb[n - d];
allpass = -g * x[n] + x[n - d] + g * allpass[n - d];
entries.audio: Creates pitched resonances, diffusion, and dense algorithmic reverb from short recursive delay structures.
entries.note: Separate comb lines parallelize well, but samples inside each feedback line remain ordered unless transformed into blocks.

entries.name: Karplus–Strong / waveguide
entries.syntax: y[n] = excitation[n] + damping * 0.5 * (y[n - d] + y[n - d - 1]);
entries.audio: Turns a short burst into a plucked string or resonant tube by recirculating a filtered delay line.
entries.note: Multiple strings or delay segments parallelize; one feedback path still needs ordered block handling.

entries.name: FFT / short-time spectrum
entries.syntax:
var<workgroup> bins: array<vec2<f32>, FFT_SIZE>;
// butterfly stages + workgroupBarrier()
entries.audio: Transforms blocks of samples into complex frequency bins for analysis and spectral processing.
entries.note: Requires windowing, overlap, bit-reversal or Stockham staging, and synchronization in uniform control flow.

entries.name: Spectral bin remap
entries.syntax: outBins[targetBin] += inBins[sourceBin] * gain;
entries.audio: Moves, mirrors, quantizes, deletes, or redistributes frequency components before inverse transformation.
entries.note: Needs FFT input and careful write coordination—prefer gather patterns or atomics when many sources share a target.

entries.name: Phase-vocoder transport
entries.syntax: phaseOut[k] += expectedAdvance + principalArg(phaseIn[k] - phasePrev[k] - expectedAdvance);
entries.audio: Separates time movement from pitch by tracking and rebuilding the phase of STFT bins.
entries.note: Requires overlapping analysis/synthesis windows, previous phase per bin, and careful transient handling.

entries.name: Envelope + dynamics reduction
entries.syntax:
energy = subgroupAdd(sample * sample);
level = sqrt(energy / f32(blockSize));
entries.audio: Measures block loudness for compression, limiting, ducking, normalization, or side-chain control.
entries.note: A smooth compressor also needs attack/release memory across blocks. Subgroup availability and size are implementation-dependent.

entries.name: Biquad / recursive IIR
entries.audio: Implements efficient low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, notch, peak, and shelving responses with two poles and two zeros.
entries.note: One stream is serial in direct form. GPU approaches use state-space block transforms, parallel scans, or many independent channels/voices.

entries.name: State-variable filter
entries.audio: Produces related low-, band-, and high-pass outputs from one resonant state update.
entries.note: Coefficient range and numerical stability depend on the discretization. Oversampling is common at high cutoff or resonance.

entries.name: Parallel scan for recurrences
entries.syntax:
// express each sample as an affine state transform
// combine transforms with an associative workgroup scan
entries.audio: Rearranges certain recursive filters or smoothers so a block can be evaluated in parallel while preserving ordered results.
entries.note: The recurrence must have a composable state transform. Workgroup barriers require uniform control flow, and state still passes between blocks.

entries.name: Overlap-add / overlap-save
entries.syntax:
windowed = inputBlock * analysisWindow;
output[offset + i] += inverseTransform(process(transform(windowed)))[i] * synthesisWindow[i];
entries.audio: Reassembles windowed or convolved blocks into a continuous stream without audible seams.
entries.note: Window, hop size, and normalization must satisfy reconstruction. Avoid write races with separate overlap buffers, atomics, or gather-style assembly.

entries.name: Partitioned FFT convolution
entries.syntax:
Y[k] = sum(partitionSpectrum[p][k] * delayedInputSpectrum[p][k]);
// IFFT + overlap-add
entries.audio: Applies very long room, cabinet, resonator, or HRTF impulse responses with bounded block latency.
entries.note: Small early partitions reduce latency; larger late partitions improve efficiency. The spectrum history and overlap tail persist across dispatches.

entries.name: Feedback delay network
entries.syntax:
let returned = feedbackMatrix * delayOutputs;
delayInputs = injection + dampingFilter(returned);
entries.audio: Couples several delay lines through a stable matrix to create dense, controllable late reverberation.
entries.note: Use an energy-preserving or deliberately lossy matrix, decorrelated delay lengths, and frequency-dependent damping. Each block carries line state forward.

entries.name: Grain-parallel sample engine
entries.audio: Scales granular synthesis from a small per-sample loop to hundreds or thousands of independent playheads over large recordings.
entries.note: GPU audio benchmarks stress this exact combination of large-buffer random access and output mixing. Memory locality and tail latency can dominate.

entries.name: Voice / layer mix reduction
entries.audio: Combines many independently rendered voices, grains, modes, or spatial paths into the final output channels.
entries.note: A one-thread-per-output design needs no reduction but limits parallelism across voices. Atomics, subgroups, or staged tree sums trade cost and determinism.

entries.name: Massive additive oscillator bank
entries.audio: Turns very large collections of sinusoids into resynthesis, spectral models, swarms, and physically derived radiation fields.
entries.note: GPU research has demonstrated real-time additive synthesis at million-sinusoid scale. Practical WebGPU designs must still budget bandwidth, reduction, and output transfer.

entries.name: Large modal resonator bank
entries.syntax:
modes[m] = amplitude[m] * exp(-decay[m] * t) * sin(phase[m]);
// parallel modes, reduce to output channels
entries.audio: Represents objects and resonant systems as hundreds or thousands of damped modes excited by impacts or continuous forces.
entries.note: Modes are embarrassingly parallel until mixing. Prune inaudible modes, fade near Nyquist, and group shared decay or spatial radiation data.

entries.name: Nonlinear string FDTD
entries.syntax: next[i] = 2.0*current[i] - previous[i] + tension*laplacian(current, i) - loss*velocity(i) + nonlinearForce(i);
entries.audio: Simulates displacement along a stiff or nonlinear string, including dispersion, tension changes, loss, and distributed excitation.
entries.note: The time step and grid spacing must satisfy stability conditions. Boundary rules, pickup position, and nonlinear terms define much of the instrument.

entries.name: 2D membrane / plate FDTD
entries.syntax: next[x,y] = 2.0*current[x,y] - previous[x,y] + c2 * laplacian2D(current, x, y) - damping * velocity(x,y);
entries.audio: Simulates drums, membranes, plates, and continuously deformable resonant surfaces on a spatial grid.
entries.note: Each time step is parallel across cells, but many ordered steps are needed per audio block. Stability, boundary shape, and pickup sampling are critical.

entries.name: Room wavefield simulation
entries.syntax: next[cell] = waveStep(neighbors, current[cell], previous[cell], material[cell], sources[cell]);
entries.audio: Propagates acoustic pressure through a 2D or 3D scene so reflections, diffraction, occlusion, and moving boundaries emerge from geometry.
entries.execution: Grid-parallel · many time steps + large state
entries.note: Audio-rate room simulation is computationally and memory intensive; grid resolution limits the highest trustworthy frequency. GPU-friendly solvers make it increasingly practical.

entries.name: Digital waveguide mesh
entries.syntax:
junctionOut[j,d] = scattering(junctionIn[j], impedance[j], d);
// propagate each outgoing wave to a neighboring junction
entries.audio: Routes traveling waves through a network of scattering junctions to model strings, plates, tubes, and connected resonant spaces.
entries.note: Junction updates parallelize, while propagation and boundary conditions require staged buffers. Dispersion and topology influence both accuracy and character.

entries.name: HRTF binaural convolution
entries.syntax:
left = convolve(source, hrtfLeft[direction]);
right = convolve(source, hrtfRight[direction]);
entries.audio: Filters a source for each ear using direction-dependent head and pinna responses, creating headphone-localized 3D sound.
entries.note: Moving sources need interpolation or crossfades between HRTFs. Dataset convention, near-field behavior, and listener personalization affect localization.

entries.name: Ambisonic speaker / binaural decode
entries.syntax:
speaker[s] = dot(decodeRow[s], soundfield);
// or convolve soundfield channels with binaural decoder filters
entries.audio: Converts an encoded sound field into loudspeaker feeds or headphone signals while preserving directional relationships.
entries.note: Higher orders improve spatial resolution but multiply channels and filter work. Decode matrices depend on speaker layout and normalization convention.

entries.name: Sliding phase vocoder
entries.audio: Continuously analyzes and rebuilds partial trajectories with finer temporal updates than a conventional frame-at-a-time phase vocoder.
entries.note: GPU spectral-processing research uses sliding and additive variants to trade latency, time resolution, and compute. Stable phase tracking remains essential.

entries.name: Spectral gate / denoiser
entries.syntax:
let gain = smoothstep(noiseFloor[k], noiseFloor[k] + knee, magnitude[k]);
outBins[k] = inBins[k] * gain;
entries.audio: Attenuates low-energy frequency bins to remove noise, isolate partials, or make spectra flicker and fragment.
entries.note: Hard independent thresholds create musical noise. Time/frequency smoothing, floor estimation, and overlap reconstruction determine quality.

entries.name: ShaderToy-style audio texture
entries.syntax:
let spectrum = textureLoad(audioTexture, vec2<i32>(bin, 0), 0).x;
let waveform = textureLoad(audioTexture, vec2<i32>(sample, 1), 0).x;
entries.audio: Exposes an external audio spectrum and waveform as shader-readable rows for reactive synthesis, modulation, and audiovisual coupling.
entries.note: ShaderToy conventionally supplies a 512×2 audio input texture; a WebGPU engine must compute or acquire that analysis and upload it explicitly.

entries.name: Compute-to-audio streaming bridge
entries.syntax:
let t = timeOffset + f32(global_invocation_id.x) / sampleRate;
outSamples[global_invocation_id.x] = vec2<f32>(left(t), right(t));
entries.audio: Defines the contract that turns parallel shader invocations into ordered stereo blocks that an audio device can play continuously.
entries.note: WebGPU is not itself an audio output API. Chunk size, queue-ahead, mapping/readback, device contention, and worst-case latency decide whether the stream is reliable.

entries.name: Parallel phase integration
entries.syntax: phase[n] = phaseAtBlockStart + prefixSum(frequency[0..n] / sampleRate);
entries.audio: Integrates arbitrary time-varying frequency into correct continuous oscillator phase for glides, FM trajectories, and control-rate pitch streams.
entries.note: Analytic envelopes can be integrated directly; arbitrary arrays need a workgroup/hierarchical scan and a phase carry between blocks. Subgroups are optional.

entries.name: Hybrid / non-uniform convolution
entries.audio: Keeps immediate reflections responsive while processing a very long reverberant tail with progressively larger FFT partitions.
entries.execution: Multi-rate blocks · direct FIR + FFT tiers
entries.note: Lower latency costs more scheduling and several partition sizes. Each tier needs its own frequency-domain delay line and overlap state.

entries.name: Oversample → nonlinear → decimate
entries.audio: Moves alias products from clipping, folding, rectification, and nonlinear filters into a wider temporary band before removing them.
entries.execution: Block/state · polyphase FIR + expanded sample rate
entries.note: Typical factors of 2×–8× multiply math and memory work. Interpolation and decimation filters carry history and add latency.

entries.name: Filtered-noise spectral synthesis
entries.syntax:
bins[k] = randomComplex(k, frame) * targetMagnitude[k];
// Hermitian mirror → IFFT → overlap-add
entries.audio: Synthesizes breath, wind, bow noise, room air, and evolving textures from a drawn or learned magnitude spectrum.
entries.note: A real signal needs Hermitian symmetry. Interpolate spectra across frames and overlap windows to prevent zippering and block seams.

entries.name: Vocoder / spectral envelope transfer
entries.syntax:
carrierBins[k] *= smoothEnvelope(abs(modulatorBins), k);
// inverse transform + overlap-add
entries.audio: Imposes the moving spectral envelope of one sound onto another, producing speech-like carriers and cross-synthesized hybrids.
entries.note: Envelope resolution, temporal smoothing, phase strategy, and window reconstruction determine intelligibility and artifacts.

entries.name: Look-ahead / true-peak limiter
entries.audio: Protects the output from peaks by inspecting future samples before their delayed playback position reaches the gain stage.
entries.note: Look-ahead adds latency. True-peak estimation requires oversampled interpolation, and smooth release needs state across blocks.

entries.name: Neural dilated-convolution block
entries.syntax: hidden = activation(conv1dDilated(input, weights, dilation) + bias);
entries.audio: Runs learned amplifier, cabinet, distortion, denoising, or timbre transformations over audio blocks.
entries.note: Model size, receptive field, intermediate memory, and latency matter. shader-f16 can help but is an optional WebGPU feature and needs a fallback.

entries.name: Neural recurrent / LSTM model
entries.syntax:
let nextState = lstmCell(inputFrame, previousState, weights);
let y = outputLayer(nextState.hidden);
entries.audio: Models stateful nonlinear hardware or temporal sound behavior whose current output depends on a compact learned memory.
entries.execution: Time-serial per stream · batch-parallel across models
entries.note: One model's recurrent time steps remain ordered, but voices, channels, or patch candidates can run in parallel. State must persist between chunks.

entries.name: DDSP harmonic + noise decoder
entries.syntax:
let parameters = neuralControl(features);
let y = harmonicBank(parameters) + filteredNoise(parameters) + reverberation(parameters);
entries.audio: Combines interpretable oscillator and noise synthesis with learned control trajectories for timbre transfer and expressive resynthesis.
entries.note: Frequency trajectories require phase integration; noise usually uses inverse FFT frames; reverb adds state. The interpretable decoder remains editable after learning.

entries.name: Mirrored-domain time field
entries.syntax: x = abs(fract(x * symmetry + offset) * 2.0 - 1.0);
entries.audio: Tiles and reflects a step coordinate into nested, palindromic note orderings. Repeating the fold creates self-similar phrases without storing a note list.
entries.note: The coordinate comes from absolute sample time, so changing GPU chunk size does not restart the pattern. Smoothed step edges keep the derived gate click-safe.

entries.name: Signed shape-boundary clock
entries.syntax:
let d = abs(sdShape(point));
let gate = 1.0 - smoothstep(band, band + edge, d);
entries.audio: Sweeps a point through circles, boxes, diamonds, hexagons, rings, or crosses. Every contour crossing becomes a musical event.
entries.note: Circle and box use conventional signed distances; the other formulas are shape-relative signed fields. A calibrated extent keeps every shape contour inside its cell, and a transition band avoids a hard gate edge.

entries.name: Polar-kaleidoscope clock
entries.syntax: let wedge = abs(fract((angle + rotation) * sectors) * 2.0 - 1.0);
entries.audio: Divides a circular traversal into reflected angular wedges, making radial symmetry audible as mirrored and palindromic pitch motion.
entries.note: Sector count changes symmetry while angular stride changes traversal order; these are independent musical controls, analogous to choosing a polygon and then a star-polygon path through it.

entries.name: Voronoi site / border event field
entries.syntax:
nearest = min(nearest, abs(site - time));
let border = 0.5 * (secondNearest - nearest);
entries.audio: Treats jittered feature sites as irregular hits, or uses the F2−F1 ridge between neighboring sites as a complementary rhythm.
entries.note: Sites remain deterministic for a seed, and the nearest and second-nearest distances provide two structurally related event streams. The bounded search keeps work predictable.

entries.name: Truchet-path clock
entries.syntax:
let arc = abs(length(local - corner) - radius);
let gate = 1.0 - smoothstep(width, width + edge, arc);
entries.audio: Scans deterministically oriented quarter-circle tiles; proximity to paired corner arcs creates syncopated gates and repeatable pitch identities.
entries.execution: Per sample · tile hash + two arc distances
entries.note: Tile orientation is discrete, but the scan coordinate and arc distance are continuous. A wandering scan lane reveals different parts of one fixed topology instead of randomizing every hit.

entries.name: KIFS recursive-fold clock
entries.syntax: for (var i = 0u; i < iterations; i++) { point = rotate(abs(point), angle) * zoom - offset; }
entries.audio: Maps a circular time path through repeated absolute-value, rotation, scale, and translation folds. Nested field regions become self-similar notes and rests.
entries.note: Iteration count is a structural parameter, not merely detail: it changes how many nested regions can be reached. Coordinates are clamped to keep extreme zooms finite.

entries.name: Interference-lattice clock
entries.syntax:
field += cos(TAU * wrappedTurns(dot(point, axis) * frequency + phase));
let gate = smoothstep(threshold, threshold + edge, field);
entries.audio: Samples the sum of rotated plane waves along an orbit. Their constructive interference becomes a quasi-periodic event lattice with longer cycles than a single grid.
entries.note: Axis count sets rotational symmetry, spatial frequency sets band density, and threshold controls event sparsity. Incommensurate rotations create long recurrence without mutable sequencer state.

entries.name: Phase-plane trajectory
entries.audio: Generates two continuous coordinates from absolute sample time. X and Y can be patched independently into spatial pattern modules.
entries.execution: Per sample · analytic X/Y control pair
entries.note: The optional input is phase displacement, not arbitrary rate modulation: integrating an unknown rate CV would require ordered state. Parameter changes are graph-crossfaded.

entries.name: Tile + mirror coordinate field
entries.syntax:
let cellPhase = fract(rotatedPoint * repeats);
let local = abs(cellPhase * 2.0 - 1.0);
entries.audio: Transforms incoming X/Y into repeated local coordinates. Mirroring makes cell boundaries continuous and turns one-way travel into forward/reverse motifs.
entries.execution: Per sample · rotation + fract + optional reflection
entries.note: Unmirrored saw coordinates jump at cell seams; mirrored triangle coordinates meet continuously. Repeat X and Y set two independent recurrence densities.

entries.name: Polar-fold coordinate field
entries.audio: Converts X/Y into continuous radius plus repeated, reflected angle. Sector symmetry and radial twist become separately patchable controls.
entries.execution: Per sample · length + atan2 + angular fold
entries.note: Reflected sectors meet continuously; non-reflected angular repetition has a seam. The angle output fades near the origin, where atan2 has no stable direction.

entries.name: Patchable signed-shape field
entries.syntax:
let distance = sdShape(repeatedPoint, shape, size);
let gate = 1.0 - smoothstep(band, band + softness, abs(distance));
entries.audio: Accepts X/Y and optional extent CV, then outputs a signed field and contour gate for circles, boxes, diamonds, hexagons, rings, or crosses.
entries.execution: Per sample · repeated analytic shape field
entries.note: The selected shape calibrates the extent range to its cell. Circle and box are conventional distances; other contours use shape-relative signed fields. The gate uses explicit softness because fragment-stage fwidth derivatives are unavailable here.

entries.name: SDF boolean / smooth logic
entries.audio: Combines two distance streams as geometric OR, AND, subtraction, or exclusive regions, then emits a new distance and gate.
entries.note: Distance-field logic differs from multiplying binary gates: it preserves proximity to the new composite contour, so thickness and smoothing remain meaningful downstream.

entries.name: Patchable interference field
entries.syntax:
field += cos(TAU * wrappedTurns(dot(point, direction) * frequency + phase));
gate = smoothstep(threshold - softness, threshold + softness, normalizedField);
entries.audio: Accepts X/Y and phase CV, then returns continuous wave interference plus an event envelope at constructive peaks.
entries.note: The continuous output is centered before gain and bias; the gate is normalized to 0–1. Axis count and threshold remain independent symmetry and density controls.

entries.name: Patchable Voronoi event field
entries.syntax:
// fixed 3x3 F1/F2 search
let eventDistance = select(sqrt(f1), 0.5 * (sqrt(f2) - sqrt(f1)), borderMode);
entries.audio: Accepts X/Y and cell-motion CV, then emits a held nearest-cell identity plus a site-center or shared-border gate.
entries.execution: Per sample · fixed local 3×3 feature search
entries.note: The bounded neighborhood provides local F1/F2; at maximum jitter it is not a global F2 proof. Border mode hashes the unordered nearest-cell pair, and width maps into separate useful site and ridge ranges.

entries.name: Patchable Truchet arc router
entries.syntax: let arcDistance = min(abs(length(local - cornerA) - radius), abs(length(local - cornerB) - radius));
entries.audio: Accepts X/Y and turn CV, then outputs tile identity and a gate along paired circular arcs in deterministic tiles.
entries.execution: Per sample · cell hash + two arc distances
entries.note: Radius 0.5 makes neighboring arcs meet at edge midpoints. The gate still closes briefly at tile seams before identity changes, preventing a held oscillator from jumping while the VCA is open.

entries.name: Hexagonal / triangular lattice crossings
entries.audio: Changes square-grid timing into three-axis recurrence. Lattice-line crossings become interlocking accents and cell identity can choose note or articulation.
entries.note: The 60-degree basis couples X and Y rates differently from a rectangular grid. Mirrored local coordinates keep repeated motifs continuous at cell boundaries.

entries.name: Logarithmic-spiral event field
entries.syntax:
let radius = max(length(point), 0.0001);
let phase = fract((atan2(point.y, point.x) + turns * log(radius)) / TAU);
entries.audio: Produces nested events at geometric radial intervals. Moving inward or outward creates accelerating or decelerating structures without changing a conventional tempo clock.
entries.note: Clamp radius away from zero. The field is scale-invariant: multiplying radius shifts phase rather than changing the pattern's local form.

entries.name: Domain-warp microtiming field
entries.audio: Bends a regular trajectory coherently across phrase, beat, and microtiming scales instead of adding unrelated random jitter to each event.
entries.note: Low noise octaves move phrases; high octaves move edges and can become audio-rate roughness. Bound octave count and phase gradient to control aliasing.

entries.name: Fractal orbit-trap events
entries.syntax: for (var i = 0u; i < iterations; i++) { z = abs(z) / max(dot(z, z), epsilon) - offset; trap = min(trap, abs(length(z) - target)); }
entries.audio: Turns minimum recursive distance, escape iteration, or region identity into sparse gates and nonlinear control gestures.
entries.execution: Per sample · bounded recursive fold loop
entries.note: This is stateless but substantially heavier than an analytic contour. Singularities need clamps, and iteration or region identity changes should be enveloped before audio use.

entries.name: Cellular-automaton score lattice
entries.syntax:
let neighborhood = (left << 2u) | (center << 1u) | right;
next[cell] = (rule >> neighborhood) & 1u;
entries.audio: Uses successive automaton generations as gate lanes, scale masks, routing matrices, or note rows. Rule number changes compositional behavior rather than one continuous intensity.
entries.execution: Ordered generations · conditional ping-pong GPU state
entries.note: Cells within one generation are parallel, but generation N+1 cannot begin before N is complete. The modular synth allocates its ping-pong rows only while a Cellular Automaton Score node is present.

entries.name: Reaction–diffusion score lattice
entries.syntax:
nextA = a + (diffA * lapA - a * b * b + feed * (1.0 - a)) * dt;
nextB = b + (diffB * lapB + a * b * b - (kill + feed) * b) * dt;
entries.audio: Evolves spots, stripes, splits, and moving chemical boundaries that can be scanned as slow CV, stereo paths, event density, or spectral weights.
entries.note: Feed and kill select qualitative regimes rather than simple amounts. Whole-grid generations use ordered passes, and the modular synth releases the surface after its last Reaction–Diffusion node is removed.

entries.name: Geometric feedback / delay lattice
entries.syntax: next[cell] = injection[cell] + decay * previous[warp(cell)] + coupling * neighborMean(previous, cell);
entries.audio: Stores audio energy in cells, then uses tiling, folds, permutations, and diffusion as feedback routing. The geometry becomes a resonant memory rather than a clock.
entries.execution: Persistent storage · conditional ordered history pass
entries.note: Decay plus coupling remain energy-bounded. The lattice stays GPU-resident while the node is active, is destroyed when unused, and does not add an intermediate CPU readback.

entries.name: Spectral signed-distance field
entries.audio: Treats frequency bins and successive analysis frames as a geometric plane. Circles, boxes, rings, crosses, or spirals keep and suppress moving regions before resynthesis.
entries.execution: 64-band workgroup DFT and overlap-add · conditional GPU spectral state
entries.note: The transform needs analysis history and overlap state, so the result has block latency. Its GPU buffers exist only while a Spectral SDF node is active and remain off the CPU until the final stereo chunk.

entries.name: Flow-field advection
entries.audio: Moves a persistent particle cloud through a curl-like field, then reduces its centroid and anisotropy to correlated X/Y controls for pitch, phase, pan, or routing.
entries.execution: Bounded particle update + aggregate interpolation · conditional GPU state
entries.note: The ordered state pass updates as many as 256 particles, reduces the old and new clouds once, then interpolates their aggregate controls across the audio chunk. Its buffers are released after the last Flow-field node is removed.

entries.name: Raymarched SDF resonator
entries.syntax:
for (var step = 0u; step < MAX_STEPS; step++) { distance += sdShape(origin + direction * distance); }
modeHz = speedOfSound / max(distance * bodySize, epsilon);
entries.audio: Turns bounded ray distances and surface identities from an implicit shape into a bank of resonant frequencies, decay weights, and stereo positions.
entries.execution: Bounded SDF ray projection · compact modal recurrence
entries.note: Ray count, march steps, and modes are strictly bounded. Unlike the grid simulations, it keeps only a small modal state bank; that bank is released when the module is absent.

entries.name: Batch-of-patches renderer
entries.audio: Auditions or exports hundreds of synth parameterizations at once, using the GPU as a parallel sound-discovery laboratory.
entries.execution: Patch × sample grid · batched output buffers
entries.note: Group similar graph topologies to reduce branch divergence and cap output/readback volume. This is often better suited to preview tiles or offline search than one live stream.
